name: paper_transformerfb
description: Canonical transformer-feedback LNA: a common-source input transistor (M1, AC-coupled gate via C1, gate-biased via R1) whose drain load is a transformer primary winding (L1, to VDD); the secondary winding (L2, one terminal AC-grounded) couples feedback via C2 back to the gate, providing simultaneous wideband input matching and noise cancellation without a purely resistive feedback path's extra noise contribution.

cited_paper.title: Design and Analysis of CMOS LNAs with Transformer Feedback for Wideband Input Matching and Noise Cancellation
cited_paper.authors: Liang Wu, Hiu Fai Leung, Howard C. Luong
cited_paper.journal: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers
cited_paper.open_access: NO -- IEEE Xplore, paywalled. Cited by title/authors/venue only; full text was not fetched or read.
cited_paper.what_was_actually_read: Only the title, authors, and venue metadata (via web search), not the paper's text or figures. The circuit transcribed here is the CANONICAL/textbook transformer-feedback LNA topology that this family of papers describes in general (drain-load primary winding, secondary winding feeding back to the gate), not a reproduction of this specific paper's exact schematic, sizing, or process node.

transcription.route: Authored directly in AnalogGenie native format; validated through upstream build_connection_matrix/dfs_all_paths (execed read-only) -> token sequence -> lna/topology.py screen -> lna/to_spice.py -> ngspice.
transcription.vocabulary_limitation_disclosed: AnalogGenie's device vocabulary (see lna/topology.py DEV_PREFIXES / lna/build_lna_corpus.py) has NO transformer or mutual-inductance primitive -- inductors are plain 2-terminal L elements with no coupling-coefficient concept at all. A transformer is therefore represented here as two GALVANICALLY SEPARATE inductors (L1 = primary, L2 = secondary) positioned exactly where the real windings sit in the signal path (drain load and gate-feedback node respectively). This reproduces the transformer-feedback topology's CONNECTIVITY correctly but cannot, even in principle within this vocabulary, encode the magnetic coupling itself -- true of every transformer-based design that could ever be added to this corpus, not specific to this circuit. Flagged explicitly for whoever works on vocabulary extensions next.

transcription_confidence: MEDIUM. The topology FAMILY and general structure (CS input stage, transformer primary as drain load, secondary feeding back to the gate) are HIGH confidence -- this is the standard, widely-taught description of transformer-feedback LNAs, cross-checked against multiple search results beyond just this one paper. Confidence is capped at MEDIUM because (a) the specific cited paper's full text/schematic was not read (paywalled), so this is a generic-family transcription attributed to a real, correctly-cited paper on that family rather than a verified reproduction of that paper's exact circuit, and (b) the vocabulary limitation above means the transformer's coupling is structurally represented but not physically modeled.
ambiguous_or_uncertain: Exact secondary-winding polarity/dot convention (affects whether feedback is positive or negative) -- not resolvable without reading the actual paper; a plausible, standard connectivity was chosen.
No component values (paywalled); to_spice.py's standard placeholder .param defaults were used.

validation.structural_screen: 5/5 -- all criteria pass (2 inductors / 6 devices = 33% ratio; 6 devices).
validation.ngspice_sim: clean run, op + sp(1-4GHz) + noise, zero errors. S11min=-0.18dB, S21max=-4.15dB with generic placeholder sizing (best S21 among the unsized transcriptions besides paper_noisecancel).

excluded_paper_check: Independent of, and unrelated to, the Kanchetla et al. TMTT 2022 paper this pipeline is blind-reproducing. Different authors (HKUST/CityU), different application focus (general wideband LNA design methodology, not a specific GNSS receiver), 2017 publication.
